items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to prohibiting
cosmetic products and personal care products that contain mercury
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8291

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
prohibiting cosmetic products and personal care products that contain
mercury

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To prohibit the distribution and sale of any cosmetic, toiletries, or
fragrances containing mercury in stores or through internet sales.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends the Environmental Conservation law by
either adding a new section or new title.

Section 2 of the bill presents the statement of findings that reinforce
the need to ban products containing mercury as an ingredient.

Section 3 of the bill sets forth definitions to give context to specific
terms.

Section 4 of the bill prohibits the distribution or sale of any cosmet-
ic, toiletries, or fragrances containing mercury in stores or through
Internet sales and sets a penalty for any person found to be selling or
distributing mercury containing cosmetics.

Section 5 of the bill requires that any cosmetics, toiletries, or
fragrances containing mercury be clearly and conspicuously labeled and
disclosed to consumers on labels, company websites, and online sites.

Section 6 of the bill adds an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Advertisers and marketers often promote and reinforce a bias toward
lighter, more Caucasian skin tones as a more desirable beauty standard.
In contrast, individuals with darker skin tones are underrepresented and
often excluded from visibility. Striving to reach these unattainable
ideals, people of color are purchasing skin lightening products contrib-
uting to a now developing billion-dollar international industry, esti-
mated to be worth $31.2 billion by 2024. Skin-lightening products do not
just subconsciously perpetuate a beauty ideal based in colorism, which
is the practice of showing preference to those of a lighter skin color
within groups of people of the same race or ethnic background, but also
these cosmetics and creams also contain toxic ingredients. When absorbed
in the skin, it can cause kidney damage, skin rashes, psychosis, skin
discoloration, and peripheral neuropathy. Mercury is the main ingredient
used in skin-lightening products to stop the production of melanin. Even
more, it is inexpensive and produces rapid results. Manufacturers place
mercury in cosmetics to fade dark spots, blemishes, fine lines, and
lighten skin. However, mercury has a high absorption rate that can
quickly damage skin and even organs.

The Minamata Convention on Mercury establishes a limit of lmg/kg (lppm)
for skin-lightening products. Many states have passed legislation
prohibiting cosmetics containing mercury and larger brands such as
Amazon have removed all skin-lightening products.  Still, the products
are easily obtainable. The United States Food and Drug Administration
(FDA) have difficulty regulating the sale of mercury-containing cosmet-
ics because most products are manufactured abroad and sold illegally in
the United States. Latino, Asian, African, and Middle Eastern communi-
ties are target customers.  Therefore, many black and brown communities
will have aisles of cosmetics with skin-lightening creams readily avail-
able for purchase.

This legislation bans the distribution and sale of any cosmetics, toile-
tries, or fragrances containing mercury in stores or through internet
sales. Additionally, this legislation further mandates that any person
manufacturing skin-lightening products containing mercury must clearly
and conspicuously disclose the level of mercury in each product. Any
manufacturer who fails to disclose the level of mercury in skin-lighten-
ing products may face penalties and fines.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The act shall take effect immediately after enactment.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8291A
 
SPONSOR: BROUK
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
prohibiting cosmetic products and personal care products that contain
mercury

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to prohibit the sale or offer for sale of
any cosmetic product or personal care product containing mercury.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 37-0117 of the environmental
conservation law to prohibit the sale or offer for sale any cosmetic
product or personal care product containing mercury.  Mercury would be
defined to mean elemental mercury Hg, mercuric iodide, mercury oxide,
mercurous, chloride, ethyl mercury, phenyl mercuric salts, ammoniated
mercury, amide chloride of mercury, mercury sulfide or cinnabaris, or
mercury iodide.

Section 2 of this bill provides that the bill shall take effect June 1,
2023.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Advertisers and marketers often promote and reinforce a bias toward
lighter, more Caucasian skin tones as a more desirable beauty standard.
Striving to reach these unattainable ideals, people of color are
purchasing skin lightening products contributing to a now developing
billion-dollar international industry, estimated to be worth $31.2
billion by 2024. Skin-lightening products do not just subconsciously
perpetuate a beauty ideal based in colorism, which is the practice of
showing preference to those of a lighter skin color within groups of
people of the same race or ethnic background, but also these cosmetics
and creams also contain toxic ingredients. When absorbed in the skin, it
can cause kidney damage, skin rashes, psychosis, skin discoloration, and
peripheral neuropathy. Mercury is the main ingredient used in skin-
lightening products to stop the production of melanin. Manufacturers
place mercury in cosmetics to fade dark spots, blemishes, fine lines,
and lighten skin. However, mercury has a high absorption rate that can
quickly damage skin and even organs.

This bill would ban the sale or offer for sale of any cosmetics products
or personal care products containing mercury. The Legislature has previ-
ously prohibited other products that contain mercury, such as in certain
dental products and in thermostats.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
BUDGET IMPLICATIONS: None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect June 1, 2023.
